Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

involve verb

entail, include

also entail, bring with it, imply (entail)

classical

Ter. Eun. 59: In amōre haec omnia īnsunt vitia
Cic. N. D. 1.117: superstitiōnem … in quā inest timor inānis deōrum

īnsum, inesse, īnfuī

verb, irregular (in + sum), with in and the ablative, or the dative, conjugation

be in, be part of

Latin turns “X involves Y” round: in X inest Y, “in X there is Y”.

Other words

  • afferō, afferre, attulī, allātum — bring with it, cause

    verb, irregular (ad + ferō), conjugation · also used · classical · Ter. And. 189: Nunc hic diēs aliam vītam affert

    Of what a thing brings with it: work, worry, risk.

  • contineō, continēre, continuī, contentum — consist in, contain

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. N. D. 1.117: religiōnem, quae deōrum cultū piō continētur

    In the passive with the ablative, “to consist in”.

  • involvō, involvere, involvī, involūtum — roll up, wrap up

    verb, third conjugation · avoid · classical · Caes. BC 1.75: sinistrās sagīs involvunt (Lewis & Short)

    Classically to wrap up or envelop, and figuratively sē litterīs involvere, to bury oneself in books (Cic. Fam. 9.20.3); it never means “to include” or “to entail”.

Examples

  • In amōre haec omnia īnsunt vitia: injūriae, suspīciōnēs, inimīcitiae, indūtiae, bellum, pāx rūrsum.

    Love involves all these troubles: wrongs, suspicions, quarrels, truces, war, then peace again.Ter. Eun. 59–61

  • nōn modo superstitiōnem tollunt, in quā inest timor inānis deōrum, sed etiam religiōnem, quae deōrum cultū piō continētur

    they do away not only with superstition, which involves an empty fear of the gods, but also with religion, which consists in the pious worship of the godsCic. N. D. 1.117

See also be involved, require, include, imply.
